concepts.title: Five Year Plans and the Goals of Planning

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Five Year Plans and the Goals of Planning' refers to.
questions.a: After independence India adopted planning through Five Year Plans drafted by the Planning Commission, with goals of growth, modernisation, self-reliance and equity, and the first plan focused on agriculture while the second launched Mahalanobis heavy industry strategy.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Five Year Plans and the Goals of Planning'.
questions.a: Planning set sectoral targets through plans, and the public sector was given the command over core and heavy industries under the Industrial Policy Resolution of 1956.

questions.q: Under which section is 'Five Year Plans and the Goals of Planning' taught, and from which source text?
questions.a: Five year plans (source: keec102.txt five year plans sections)

concepts.title: Agriculture: Land Reforms, Green Revolution and Marketing

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Agriculture: Land Reforms, Green Revolution and Marketing' refers to.
questions.a: Agricultural policy combined institutional reforms of land ceiling and consolidation with the Green Revolution package of high yielding variety seeds, fertilisers and assured irrigation from the mid 1960s, plus regulated markets and minimum support price to stabilise farmer incomes.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Agriculture: Land Reforms, Green Revolution and Marketing'.
questions.a: The Green Revolution raised foodgrain output and made India self-sufficient in food, but benefited mainly well irrigated regions and larger farmers.

questions.q: Under which section is 'Agriculture: Land Reforms, Green Revolution and Marketing' taught, and from which source text?

concepts.title: Industry: Industrial Licensing and Public Private Split

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Industry: Industrial Licensing and Public Private Split' refers to.
questions.a: Industrial policy reserved core industries for the public sector, controlled private entry through industrial licensing, and channelled small scale reservation for employment, which built a broad industrial base but created inefficiency, shortage and licensing raj by the 1980s.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Industry: Industrial Licensing and Public Private Split'.
questions.a: Industrial licensing constrained private investment decisions, and small scale industry reservation aimed to protect employment intensive units.

questions.q: Under which section is 'Industry: Industrial Licensing and Public Private Split' taught, and from which source text?

concepts.title: Trade Policy: Inward Looking Import Substitution

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Trade Policy: Inward Looking Import Substitution' refers to.
questions.a: Trade policy till 1990 was inward looking, using tariffs and quotas to protect domestic industry under import substitution, which conserved foreign exchange and nurtured industry but raised costs, reduced competition and limited export growth.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Trade Policy: Inward Looking Import Substitution'.
questions.a: Tariffs are taxes on imports and quotas fix physical limits, both shielding domestic producers from foreign competition.

questions.q: Under which section is 'Trade Policy: Inward Looking Import Substitution' taught, and from which source text?
questions.a: Trade policy 1950-1990 (source: keec102.txt trade policy section)
